Looking at this barcode, I can identify the following features:

- **Fully grayscale** → eliminates the color films (Boogeyman, Exorcist III, Nosferatu '79, Manos, Day of the Dead), leaving the B&W classics: Carnival of Souls, Night of the Living Dead, House on Haunted Hill, The Last Man on Earth, Little Shop of Horrors.

- **Not Night of the Living Dead**: that film is essentially one long dark night sequence (a farmhouse at night for ~70% of the runtime), which would produce a nearly uniform very dark barcode rather than the alternating medium-gray stretches and two distinct near-black bands seen here.

- **The structure matches *House on Haunted Hill*** remarkably well:
  - Dark opening (skeleton prologue, night arrival at the house)
  - A long, busy **medium-gray stretch (~10–43%)** — the brightly lit but noir-shaded party/tour/wine-cellar sequences
  - A **very dark band (~43–54%)** — the midnight lights-out sequence with the skeleton and the ghost
  - A medium stretch (~54–76%) — the accusations, séance, and escalating scares
  - Another **very dark band (~76–89%)** — Nora's flight and the acid-vat/climax sequence
  - Medium (~89–95%) — the reveal that it was staged
  - Dark, then **one bright stripe near the very end (~98%)** — the dawn departure scene, followed by the dark "THE END" card

The two clean near-black bands surrounded by medium-gray activity, plus the bright flash right at the end, fit this film's structure better than the alternatives.
